department: Department of Physics, College of Sciences (Engineering & Applied Science Ph.D.)

deadline.value: The program's Fall deadline is July 1/July 15 for domestic applicants, so international applicants must meet the Graduate School international Fall deadline of May 19, 2027; apply by March 1, 2027 for Graduate School Awards consideration.

also.quote: Application student submission deadline (If program deadlines earlier, earliest deadline applies.) | Fall 2026 | May 19, 2026
Applied Physics, M.S., Ph.D. | Degree Requirements | College of Sciences ... Spring Admission: October 15 | Fall Admission: July 1
Apply by March 1st to be considered

gre_general.value: GRE General is required (Engineering & Applied Science Ph.D. specifies 300 combined V+Q; Physics recommends 300 V+Q and 3.5 analytical writing).
gre_general.quote: M.S. and Ph.D. Department Requirements | 3 references are required. Applicants will provide contact information within the application. | Statement of Purpose | Test Requirements: GRE

also.quote: GRE Score (combined verbal and quantitative sections) of 300, and proof of English proficiency.
Recommended minimum GRE scores are 300 (verbal + quantitative) and 3.5 on analytical writing.

gre_subject.value: Neither the Physics graduate pages nor the Engineering & Applied Science pages state a policy for the GRE Physics Subject Test.

supervisor.value: Neither the Physics graduate pages nor the Engineering & Applied Science admissions page states whether a faculty supervisor's agreement is required before admission.

funding.value: Departmental teaching assistantships (~4 new TAs/year, $1,300/month for the 9-month academic year plus tuition waiver, 20 hrs/week) and faculty grant-funded research assistantships are awarded competitively.
funding.quote: Assistantships are available to well-qualified students. Typically, the department has 4 new teaching assistantsships each year.

also.quote: Currently, stipends are $1300/month for the 9-month academic year, along with a tuition waiver.

entry_route.value: Physics Ph.D. students must hold a Master's degree in physics/engineering/a related field or complete the Physics M.S. coursework while pursuing the Ph.D. (ENAS gives preference to Master's holders while considering strong Bachelor's applicants).
entry_route.quote: Physics-based students enrolling in the interdisciplinary Ph.D. program in Engineering and Applied Science must have a Masters degree from an accredited college or university in engineering, physics, mathematics, geophysics, computer science, or other closely related field, or be willing to complete course work required in the existing Masters' programs in the Department of Physics while pursuing the degree.

also.quote: Preference will be given to students who possess a Master’s degree in the related field, but students whose Bachelor’s transcript demonstrate a strong academic performance will be considered.

notes: Applied Physics concentration within the Engineering & Applied Science Ph.D. Physics how-to-apply page cites legacy TOEFL 79 iBT / 550 PBT (university international page updates to 4.0 on the Jan 21, 2026 scale). Requires 3 references and statement of purpose; separate Program Information form required for Physics assistantships.
